entries.title: Kinky celebra 25 años de su álbum debut en Chicago
entries.summary: <p>Kinky, una de las bandas alternativas más emblemáticas de Monterrey, regresó a Chicago para celebrar 25 años de su álbum debut homónimo, llevando consigo la mezcla explosiva de rock, electrónica y ritmos que hizo a la banda pionera a nivel internacional.</p><p>El sábado pasado, Kinky tomó el escenario del Park West, en Lincoln Park, con un show dividido en dos partes: primero interpretó el álbum de principio a fin; después recorrió algunos de sus grandes éxitos y presentó su música más reciente. Entre sus nuevos temas se encuentra su sencillo de 2026, “Si no te vuelvo a ver”, que los fans han recibido con entusiasmo por su sonido nostálgico e inconfundible.</p><p>“ Tener la oportunidad de seguir los cinco juntos tocando durante tantos años, haciendo música también nueva, tocando en muchos festivales, visitando todavía ciudades nuevas, países nuevos, nos llena de emoción y seguimos con el mismo entusiasmo con el que empezamos”, dijo Ulises Lozano, miembro de la banda, a La Voz.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-890000" name="module-890000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>La banda regiomontana, integrada por César Pliego, Omar Góngora, Gil Cerezo, Carlos Chairez y Lozano, siempre se ha caracterizado por fusionar géneros como la electrónica y el rock. Su álbum debut fue, desde el principio, un reflejo de las distintas influencias musicales de sus integrantes.</p><p>En una entrevista con <a class="Link" href="https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2002-apr-20-et-gurza20-story.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com" target="_blank" ><u>Los Angeles Times</u></a>, la banda explicó que Lozano se inclinaba por la música electrónica, Góngora por el afro-jazz, Pliego por las cumbias y Cerezo por el rock. Al juntar estas influencias, Kinky creó un sonido que se sentía natural y difícil de encasillar en un sólo género. Con el tiempo, el mundo se puso a su nivel.</p><p>“ Kinky nació en base a la experimentación, a la fusión de música que en ese momento, hace 25 años, era muy raro”, dijo Lozano. “ Hoy en día es parte ya de lo que es la música en general. Ahorita ya ves regionales haciendo cosas con los rockeros, los rockeros con los poperos, los poperos con los electronic, los electrónicos con los alternative, los alternativos con lo regional nadie sabía cómo catalogar a Kinky, pero de muchas maneras, el mercado musical de Chicago también se ha adelantado a su tiempo. Actualmente, estamos viendo una ola de eventos por toda la ciudad que mezclan géneros y escenas de maneras inesperadas, desde <a class="Link" href="https://navypier.org/pier-events/punchis-punchis-banda-rave-experience/" target="_blank" ><u>raves de banda</u></a> hasta fiestas de <a class="Link" href="https://southsideweekly.com/para-los-darks-the-event-production-curating-events-for-alternative-latinos/" target="_blank" ><u>cumbia gótica</u></a>. Tambien hay bandas locales como Los Vatos Tristes, que hasta han creado términos como “mexwest emo” para definir su música.</p><p>“ Chicago es super importante para Kinky, es de las primeras ciudades que visitamos que realmente conectaron muy rápido con el sonido de Kinky”, explicó Lozano.</p><p>Y es que, ¿cómo no iba Chicago a conectar con Kinky? La ciudad donde nació el house, uno de los géneros que definieron la música electrónica, ya tenía un público acostumbrado a sonidos que rompían las barreras entre géneros, haciendo de Chicago un lugar ideal para recibir a Kinky en ese entonces y seguir conectando con su música hoy.</p><p>Chicago fue la tercera parada en este tour después de Los Ángeles y San Diego. El setlist incluyó algunos covers, como el éxito de cumbia “El paso del gigante” de Grupo Soñador, y “Fuentes de Ortiz”, una versión del tema de Ed Maverick que forma parte del EP de cinco canciones de Kinky, “5 disparos”, lanzado en 2024.</p><p>Es casi un adelanto de un proyecto especial que la banda está preparando.</p><p>“ Viene una celebración de los 25 años de Kinky, donde también vamos a entries.title: Gas prices are spiking in Chicago again. Why there may be no end in sight
entries.summary: <h3>Soaring gas prices have been a challenge since early this spring, but eventually came down. Are prices spiking again now? </h3><h3></h3><p>Yes. The nation’s average price of gasoline was $4.25 a gallon as of Sept. 14, according to <a class="Link" href="https://www.gasbuddy.com/go/oil-tops-100-diesel-crosses-6-and-gas-prices-jump-in-every-state-with-no-relief-in-sight" target="_blank" ><u>GasBuddy</u></a>. The national average is up 19 cents compared to last month and $1.14 higher per gallon than a year ago.</p><p>In Illinois, the average gas price was $4.86 on Friday, according to AAA. The national average was $4.47 on the same date. For Chicago, the <a class="Link" href="https://gasprices.aaa.com/?state=IL" target="_blank" >average price for regular gas</a> is currently $5.14, AAA said. </p><p>Gas prices nationwide have returned to the highs seen this spring after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28 over disputes about Iran's nuclear weapons program. Now the national average is closer to this year’s high of $4.56 on May 21. The all-time high for the national average is $5.01 set on June 14, 2022, said GasBuddy.</p><h3>Why are fuel prices so high?</h3><p>After the attack by the U.S. and Israel, Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow mouth of the Persian Gulf. Twenty percent of the world’s oil supply passes through the Strait.</p><p>It’s the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/economy/2026/03/25/iran-war-raising-chicago-gas-travel-medicine-food-oil-prices" target="_blank" ><u>largest disruption</u></a> the oil industry has ever faced, Sam Ori, executive director of the University of Chicago’s Institute for Climate and Sustainable Growth said this spring.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://www.iea.org/topics/the-middle-east-and-global-energy-markets" target="_blank" ><u>International Energy Agency</u></a> has said the combined impacts of the war in the Middle East and blockages in energy trade flows through the Strait amount to "the greatest threat to global energy security in history."</p><h3>Why did fuel prices spike recently?</h3><p>Average gasoline and diesel prices rose in every U.S. state last week as geopolitical tensions escalated on multiple fronts, said Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at <a class="Link" href="https://www.gasbuddy.com/go/oil-tops-100-diesel-crosses-6-and-gas-prices-jump-in-every-state-with-no-relief-in-sight" target="_blank" ><u>GasBuddy</u></a> in a Sept. 14 blog post.</p><p>Tensions are ongoing between the U.S. and <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/iran-us-war-hormuz-trump-yemen-houthis-2b126da67b09de2f328846eb656abe0e" target="_blank" ><u>Iran</u></a>. Then on Sept. 10, the Iran-backed <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/hub/houthis" target="_blank" ><u>Houthi rebel group</u></a> took over Yemen’s port city of Mokha, an area vital to controlling shipping through the Red Sea, said the <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/yemen-iran-houthi-rebels-red-sea-mokha-e4e799701b382799a955969c212800ea" target="_blank" ><u>Associated Press</u></a>. And on Sept. 11, Saudi Arabia said it had shut down the East-West pipeline after it was attacked by drones. The Saudi Foreign Ministry blamed the attack on several drones that came from Iraq, the AP reported.</p><p>In addition, Ukraine has been attacking Russian oil refineries for months. New attacks last weekend “also knocked two additional Russian refineries offline, further straining global refined product supplies and likely offsetting any seasonal relief,” said De Haan of <a class="Link" href="https://www.gasbuddy.com/go/oil-tops-100-diesel-crosses-6-and-gas-prices-jump-in-every-state-with-no-relief-in-sight" target="_blank" ><u>GasBuddy</u></a>.</p><h3>Is gas cheaper in Indiana and Wisconsin than Chicago?</h3><p>Yes, gas prices in Indiana are among the lowest in the U.S.</p><p>On Friday, Indiana’s average gas price was $4.00, said AAA. That was the second-lowest nationwide, behind Texas, which had the lowest average price in the U.S. at $3.95 on the same day.</p><p>Just north of the border in Wisconsin, the average gas price sits at $4.41, six cents below the national average and 45 cents cheaper than in Illinois, AAA said.</p><p>Illinois gas prices are often higher than the national average because it has the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/economy/2026/06/11/spiking-gas-prices-chicagoans-stop-rising-food-prices-inflation" target="_blank" ><u>second-highest taxes</u></a> on gas in the country, according to Illinois Policy. Five states, including Illinois, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/economy/2026/06/11/spiking-gas-prices-chicagoans-stop-rising-food-prices-inflation" target="_blank" >have a motor fuel tax</a>. Revenue from that tax helps maintain and build Illinois roads.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" </div><p></p><h3>Where to buy cheaper gas around Chicago? </h3><p>GasBuddy, which also has an app that tracks the lowest gas prices in a city or region, shows several areas in Indiana near Chicago where drivers can fuel up for just under the state and city average price.</p><p>A Citgo at 11600 S. Michigan Ave. in West Pullman, a Shell at 10655 S. Halsted St. in Roseland, and a BP at 4000 W. Peterson Ave. in North Park were all charging under $4.70 per gallon for regular gas on Friday, GasBuddy showed.</p><p>The app provides a list of gas stations by price and location that is updated hourly.</p><h3>Why are prices different at various gas stations?</h3><p>Gas stations, which are often independently owned, typically price fuel based on how much it would cost to replace it or how much the next shipment of fuel will cost, according to the National Association of Convenience Stores.</p><p>Within reason, retailers can set fuel prices themselves, but Chicago drivers can <a class="Link" href="https://311.chicago.gov/s/article/Fuel-pump-complaint?language=en_US" target="_blank" ><u>report suspected price gouging</u></a> to the city’s Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection.</p><h3>Will gas prices continue to rise?</h3><p>Most of the U.S. is shifting to cheaper winter-blend gasoline, but ongoing geopolitical tensions make relief unlikely in the near term. “Motorists should brace for continued volatility ahead,” said De Haan of GasBuddy.</p><h3>Think regular and premium prices are high? Diesel is even higher.</h3><p>The national average price of diesel reached $6 a gallon for the first time in history last week. “It is a level diesel has never reached, and it comes less than a week after prices set a fresh all-time record of $5.85,” said <a class="Link" href="https://www.gasbuddy.com/go/statement-on-diesel-reaching-6-per-gallon-for-the-first-time-in-history" target="_blank" ><u>GasBuddy</u></a> on Sept. 10 in a blog post.</p><p>Diesel prices could climb even higher in the wake of fresh attacks on Russian refineries.</p><p>On Friday, the national average price for diesel hit a record high of $6.45, according to AAA.</p><p>On Sunday, U.S. President Donald Trump called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to halt strikes on Russian refineries that produce diesel, But spiking diesel prices have far-reaching economic impact.</p><p>“Diesel is the fuel that moves the economy, powering the freight trucks, trains, agricultural equipment and construction machinery behind nearly everything Americans buy. That means its impact reaches far beyond the transportation sector,” GasBuddy said.</p><p>That can translate into steep prices for groceries, household goods, deliveries and other products. That’s on top of already-high inflation that <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/economy/2026/06/11/spiking-gas-prices-chicagoans-stop-rising-food-prices-inflation" target="_blank" >many are struggling with</a>.</p><p><i>Contributing: AP</i></p>
